To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

ABA regulates the expression of the LuPLRs gene, which codes for the pinoresinolariciresinolate reductase involved in the biosynthesis of the cancer-preventive compound (+)-secoisolariresinol, in both seeds and flax cell suspension cultures.
the control exerted by abscisic acid (ABA, a plant hormone) on lignan biosynthetic genes is modulated by calcium, which is a universal second messenger involved in many physiological processes.
the control exerted by abscisic acid on lignan biosyntheses in flax (L. usitatissimum) is modulated by the Ca2+ signal involving the calmoduline-like LuCML 15b.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the control of the biosynthesis of a cancer chemoprotective lignan, (+)-seco-isolariciresinols in flax.
a better understanding of the mechanisms underlying the control exerted by abscisic acid on the biosynthesis of cancer chemopreventing lignans.
the control exerted by abscisic acid on lignan biosynthetic gene expression in flax, which is modulated by the Ca2+ signal pathway involving the calmoduline-like LuCML1b protein.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ABA regulates the LuPLR gene and lignan biosynthetic pathway in flax through a Ca2+-dependent pathway involving the LuCML15 calmodulin-like protein.
Ca2+ signaling plays a key role as a mediator of the ABA-mediated control on the LuPLR pathway, which leads to the biosynthesis of the cancer chemoprevention lignan (+)-secoisoariciresinol.
ABA-mediated regulation of LuPLRL gene expression and lignans accumulation in flax is modulated by the Ca2+ signal pathway involving the calmoduline-like LuCML 15b.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Ca2+ signaling is involved in the ARA-mediated control of LuPLR expression and (+)-secoisolariresinol biosynthesis.
the control exerted by the phytohormone ABA on the biosynthesis of lignans in flax is modulated by Ca2+ signal, involving the calmoduline-like protein LuCML15.

ABA induces a rise in the cytosolic free Ca2+ concentration, which activates CaM-like proteins and CaMKII, leading to the activation of the transcription factor MYB2, which in turn binds to the ABRE and the MYB2 elements of the LuPlr1 promoter, resulting in a strong activation of the LuPLr1 expression.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ABA and Ca2+ signaling interact to control the expression of the LuPLRs1 gene involved in the biosynthesis of the cancer chemoprevention lignans in flax.
the regulation of lignan biosynthesis and accumulation in flax is mediated by a Ca2+-signaling pathway.
the control exerted by the phytohormone ABA on lignans biosynthesis in the model species flax, is modulated by the calcium signal transduction involving a calmodulin-like protein, LuCMLb.
